newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on fund long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on fund long liquidation.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Wednesday amid massive fund long liquidation prompted by ideas the market had peaked, traders said.
Technicians cited bearish chart signals while fundamental traders pointed to expectations for a low soybean export figure in Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report.

"There is a growing feeling that the market stubbed its toe last week at $9.00," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "There is obviously considerable uncertainty at these higher levels. The expectation is for some pretty low numbers on the exports tomorrow."

Traders said they expected the report to show 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of soybean exports. But some floor sources cited rumblings that the net sales figure could be negative due to cancellations and rolling of sales to new crop.
Soybeans closed 11-3/4 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower with July down 10-1/2 at $8.64 and new crop November down 5-1/4 at $7.04-1/2.

Pit sources said funds sold the opening and continued to dump soybeans throughout the morning, led by Merrill Lynch, Refco Inc and Iowa Grain. Chartists said the market had been giving off bearish signals since Monday's sharp break.
Traders said stops were hit in the July contract below $8.60 per bushel.

Fundamental factors offered little support. Trade sources said it was too early to worry about the impact below-normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest were having on seed germination and plant development. Also, Monday's USDA supply and demand report lessened concerns about tight supply.
USDA on Monday left soybean ending stocks at 125 million bushels. That was still considered tight but many had expected USDA to trim another five million to 10 million bushels.
On the day, funds sold at least 20 million bushels. Technical traders noted the July contract broke through a trend line which was viewed as a bearish move.
"We broke through a big trend line in the July beans today," a trader said. "The next downward objective is $8.45."

Prudential Securities sold six million bushels July, Refco Inc sold 4.5 million July and one million November, Iowa Grain sold 4.5 million July and Griffin Trading sold four million July, pit sources said.
In options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,250 July $7.00 puts at 1/8 to 1/4 cent and Lind-Waldock bought 1,000 July $9.75 calls at 3-7/8.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 68,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 66,309 contracts.
